findings.title: Task 7's new online prediction case assumes the replica's Hound faces heading 0, but the spawn heading depends on the seed
findings.claim: The case sends `reticle(8000)` and then expects `src().turret(0)` to be > 0 and either a multiple of 455 or exactly 8000. But `turretAim` is a world fine aim: `predictTurret` calls `slewTurret(v, t.ships[0].heading, aim, …)`. So the target offset is `turretOffset(heading, 8000)`, clamped to ±10922, and that equals 8000 only when the replica's Hound heading is 0. For most headings the offset is negative, or it is clamped, or it ends at a value that is neither 8000 nor a multiple of 455.
findings.evidence: plan L1459-1475 (reticle(8000), `expect(p).toBeGreaterThan(0); expect(p % 455 === 0 || p === 8000)`), plan L1492-1499 (predictTurret slews about `t.ships[0].heading`); map.ts L57-59 (spawnAt: heading = (first + 64) % 256, prograde), L72-73 (`first = nextInt(rng, HEADING_COUNT)`); state.ts L283 (ships at map.spawns).
findings.why: As written, the test can pass only by luck of seed 5's spawn heading, so Task 7 Step 6's expected PASS is not guaranteed. This is a test the executor cannot make pass as written.
findings.fix: Derive the reticle from the replica. Use `const h0 = c.state()!.tactical.ships[0].heading; const want = (h0 * 256 + 2000) % 65536;` and send `reticle(want)`. Then assert `p > 0 && p <= 2000 && (p % 455 === 0 || p === 2000)`. Alternatively, assert `p` equals `predictTurret(c.state()!.tactical, 0, { weaponSel: 0, turretAim: want }, true, k)` for the k the rig reached.

findings.title: Task 10's commit names tests/w4Auto.test.ts for rung 4, but the first-seated-tick test lives in tests/duelScripted.test.ts
findings.claim: The new rung-4 rule updates Task 6's 'its first seated tick sends shipPower …' case. Step 5's git add appends `<tests/w4Auto.test.ts if rung 4 is kept>`, but Task 6 puts that describe block in `tests/duelScripted.test.ts`, which the commit omits.
findings.evidence: plan L1341-1345 (the case is in tests/duelScripted.test.ts); plan L1911 (rung 4 rule); plan L1926 (commit placeholder names w4Auto.test.ts)
findings.why: If rung 4 is kept, the updated test would be left out of the tuning commit, and an unchanged file would be staged.
findings.fix: Change the placeholder to `<tests/duelScripted.test.ts if rung 4 is kept>`. Add `<tests/w4Loadout.test.ts if rung 2 is kept>` as well; it is already listed, so note that it changes only for rung 2.

findings.title: The w4Autocannon rewrite names the wrong lines: the interval case drives TRIGGER through gaps(), and the heat-lock case pins no interval
findings.claim: Task 6 Step 4 says the interval case calls `tickGun(st, 0, IDLE_INPUT, true)`. That case reaches tickGun only through the `gaps()` helper, which hard-codes `TRIGGER`. Step 4 also says to re-pin the heat-and-lock case's interval numbers to the MAN row, but that case asserts no interval.
findings.evidence: plan L1323-1324; W-4a plan L567-571 (gaps uses TRIGGER), L587-600 (heat-and-lock case: heat, lock and cooling only)
findings.why: The executor has to infer that `gaps()` itself changes, while the lock case, which needs TRIGGER in MAN, does not use `gaps()`. The re-pin instruction points at numbers that are not there.
findings.fix: Say that `gaps()` calls `tickGun(st, 0, IDLE_INPUT, true)`, along with the direct TRIGGER calls at W-4a L584, L604, L609, L616, L619 and L628. Say that the heat-and-lock case sets `s.gunsManual = true`, keeps TRIGGER and needs no re-pin.
